svg.title: Area between x = y² and x = y + 2 with one horizontal rectangle
svg.desc: The region between the parabola x = y² (crimson, on the left) and the line x = y + 2 (blue, on the right) is shaded from y = −1 to y = 2, where the curves meet at (1, −1) and (4, 2). One thin horizontal rectangle of thickness Δy runs across the region; its length is right minus left, (y + 2) − y². A side panel gives the limits from y² = y + 2, y = −1 and 2, and the area, the integral from −1 to 2 of [(y + 2) − y²] dy = 9/2. In x the bottom boundary changes at x = 1, so slicing vertically would need two integrals.
svg.text: In x, the bottom boundary changes
at x = 1, so x needs two integrals.
